definition: The position of a particle measured from a fixed point O on its line of motion, with a sign: $s < 0$ means it is on the negative side of O.
The rate of change of displacement, $v = \frac{\mathrm{d}s}{\mathrm{d}t}$. Its sign gives the direction of motion.
The rate of change of velocity, $a = \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}s}{\mathrm{d}t^{2}}$.
The magnitude of velocity, $\lvert v\rvert$: how fast a particle moves, whatever its direction, so it is never negative.
The total length of path a particle covers, counting motion in both directions as positive: $\int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} \lvert v(t)\rvert\,\mathrm{d}t$.
